h1: How to automate form filling on websites
answer: Keep the data in one list with an ID and a status per row, fill one form at a time, and submit only after you approve.
Save each confirmation back to its row.

chooser.h2: Which kind of form filling do you mean?

root.q: What do you want to fill?

options.label: My own details, on any site

then.why: Chrome fills addresses, contact details, passwords and payment methods, and each can be turned off. No automation needed.

options.label: The same snippets in many forms

then.why: It types your saved snippets on a shortcut. You still check and click submit.

options.label: One form, many times, from a list

then.answer: Use a browser agent or browser automation
then.why: It fills one row at a time and asks before each submit. Follow the steps below.

then.answer: Use an automation on the form app
then.why: Typeform, Google Forms and Jotform have triggers in automation catalogs, so no browser is needed.

method.h2: How to automate form filling, step by step

steps.title: Put the data in one list
steps.body: One row per form to fill, one column per field, plus an ID and a Status (To do, Filled, Submitted, Failed). A single list is the fix for most failures.

steps.title: Map columns to fields by label
steps.body: Write the map once: the "Company name" column goes to the "Business name" field. Labels change less than page layouts.

steps.title: Check before submit
steps.body: Required fields filled, dates in the site's format, nothing cut off. A tool that fills and then shows you the form is worth more than one that is fast.

steps.title: Submit only on approval
steps.body: A submitted form usually cannot be taken back. Approve each one, at least until a few dozen have gone through clean.

note.text: In 50agents, a browser agent alone does not read your Google Sheet. Hold the list in an app, and a browser agent in its crew works through the rows.

steps.title: Save proof
steps.body: The confirmation number, a reference, or the page title after submit, written back to the row with Status Submitted.

steps.title: Never resubmit without checking
steps.body: If a run fails after submit, look for the confirmation before trying again, or you will send it twice.

captain.line: Captain sets up a browser agent that fills the warranty form, stops, and asks you. Approve, and it submits exactly what you saw.
captain.ask: Set up a browser agent that registers each espresso machine I tell it about on the warranty form at maker.example, and asks me before it submits

wrong.title: Submitted twice
wrong.body: A retry after a slow page. Check for the confirmation before any retry, and keep the Status column true.

wrong.title: Fields shifted
wrong.body: The site added a field and everything moved down one. Map by label, and check a filled form before the first submit after any site change.

wrong.title: The wrong row
wrong.body: Two rows share a name. Give each row an ID and show it in the approval.

wrong.title: A form on a look-alike site
wrong.body: Personal data went to the wrong address. Fill forms only on the exact address in your list.

wrong.title: A CAPTCHA appears
wrong.body: The site does not want automated submits. Do not use CAPTCHA bypass; ask the site for a bulk upload or an API instead.

faqs.q: How do I fill the same web form many times automatically?
faqs.a: Keep the data in a sheet with one row per form, and use a browser automation tool or browser agent to fill one row at a time. Submit only after a check, and save the confirmation to the row.

faqs.q: Can I fill a web form from a spreadsheet?
faqs.a: Yes. That is the most reliable setup: the sheet is the source, the tool fills from it and writes the result back.

faqs.q: What about forms with a CAPTCHA?
faqs.a: Stop there. A CAPTCHA is the site asking for a person. Do those by hand, or ask the site for a bulk option.
Map columns to fields by their label, not their position, because labels change less than layouts. When a field is not found, the run should stop and tell you, not guess.
Many tools can attach a file to an upload field if the file is reachable, for example a link in the row. Test it on one row and check the confirmation before running the rest.

faqs.q: How do I avoid submitting twice?
faqs.a: Give each row an ID and a Status, and save the confirmation number back to the row. If a run fails after submit, look for that confirmation before you try again.
